answer: The gate stays shut to ghosts because the toll is real. Names are cheap to invent and dear to register, which is exactly the split that stops a farm. Before the stamp comes an examination charge of £22, charged again each time a name fails, and a name that cannot pay it never gets stamped. One name, one proof, one entry: Entered cart driver stable charter enforces it, and a charter drivers file after cart hearings is how the check runs. The tally keeps nectar.
